about: ASR stage recomputed from marks the run already wrote; no rerun, no audio. A is fdbench's number (VAD end -> transcript). B adds endpointing, which is what the deck wording 'end of speech -> transcript' promises. C/D use the streaming model's last interim: when the text already existed, before the second pass.

B_speech_end_to_mark.label: B  true speech end -> transcript (deck wording)

C_speech_end_to_partial.label: C  true speech end -> last streaming partial

D_vad_end_to_partial.label: D  VAD end -> last streaming partial

E_whisper_pass.label: E  whisper second pass alone (log clock)

streaming_only.note: How much of the reported ASR stage is the streaming recogniser and how much is the optional second pass. D < 0 means the streaming text was already complete before the VAD declared the turn over, so the recogniser contributes no stage latency at all.

counterfactual.note: If ASR_FINAL_PASS were 'none' (answer on the streaming text): true speech end -> reply audio = endpointing + TTFT + TTFB + handoff, per turn. The ASR term goes to zero because the streaming text is already complete at vad_end; endpointing still applies, since the aggregator triggers on the VAD stop. Arithmetic on measured values, not a run.

wer.note: last_partial = the interim mark, often truncated mid-word, so pessimistic. streaming_flushed = what final_pass=none would actually emit. whisper_final = the transcript the run used.
